title: Amazingly effective!
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 22, 2023
review: We've been having a serious fruit fly/gnat infestation for years, and I'm almost positive they're breeding somewhere in our walls, floors or ceilings -- we've had leaks in the past, and I think we still do. So while it may take more than a trap to eradicate the gnat population here, this trap has brought us substantial relief, in just the span of 2-3 days.We can't call in the professionals at this point, for reasons I can't go into, but since the weather got warmer this spring, life in our small apartment was becoming unbearable. They were flying into our faces, landing on us, and landing in or on our food, even as we prepared it or ate it.I don't think it's been more than 48 hours, and there are A LOT of dead flies in the trap.We've caught substantial numbers with both homemade vinegar traps and the electronic Katchees, but this trap seems to summon the gnats, even from other rooms of the apartment (the trap is in the bedroom, but we also have a combination kitchen/LR, a bathroom and a foyer).Be warned, the trap does have a strict vinegar smell that wafts around, but the smell is NOTHING in comparison to the nuisance of the gnats.They do hang around the rim of the trap for a while, but then they definitely fly into it and die. We put it in an awkward place, and I don't want to take the chance of spilling it, so I can't get anything close to a count, but not only can I glimpse a large quantity of dead gnats, but I haven't seen ANY flying or landing anywhere else in our place, in many hours. This is truly amazing.I don't expect that it will eradicate them completely, because we don't know the breeding source, but one can always hope that all breeding adults will eventually fly around and find this thing. Until then, we may have to keep replacing the traps and finding ways to stretch out the liquid. Maybe we'll post an update, at some point.Meanwhile, I THANK GOD for the blessing of having this trap to control the terrible nuisance that was making our lives so unpleasant and difficult.Posting this update about 2-3 weeks later -- unfortunately in the warm weather (and we don't have air conditioning), these gnats are multiplying faster than the trap can catch them. Without it, we'd probably be swamped in gnats, fruit flies and whatever all these pests are. We'll have to put more traps around.

title: Day Spa for Fruit Flies
date: Reviewed in the United States on July 8, 2022
review: First, the product is not that easy to use. The instructions say to shake well before opening, but it creates a layer of foamy bubbles that take about 15 minutes to dissolve. While the bubbles are present, the fruit flies don't go anywhere close to it. Then the whole product is a jar of some vinegar liquid that is just supposed to be left open on the counter 24 hours a day until all the flies are trapped. It's really easy to tip/spill every where and at 5.4 fl oz, it makes a mess.Second, the scent is awful. It smells like a jar of vinegar (which I could have poured without spending money on this product) and it permeates a 5' radius of where it's located. We kept trying to figure out what was leaking before we realized it was the fruit fly trap.Third, the fruit flies think it's a day spa! They land on the rim and dip down to the top of the liquid, but don't actually fly in the trap. They just chill out around it like we've created a resort for them instead of exterminating.We have other Stem products and love them, but this one was an epic fail!

title: I was extremely dissappointed in this product
date: Reviewed in the United States on November 24, 2023
review: I read the directions twice and it is very simple. Shake real good before opening then unscrew the lid off and peel off the protective foil. Then just leave it sitting out on a counter or whatever, near where the fruit flies or gnats seem to be the worse. I would watch the fruit flies crawl all over this product kinda checking it out but it seemed they would always lose interest and go away instead of going for the liquid to get trapped. Now to be fair, I may have caught close to 50 after a couple weeks but when I saw it wasn't working to well, I broke out some fly ribbon paper I had leftover in an old box and the fly ribbon was absolutely covered with them so I won't be wasting any more money on traps like this when I can get 10pc of fly ribbon paper for real cheap. I even have a trick I use. When you hang the flypaper from the ceiling it doesn't really hang down real low and only traps the ones flying up high so I used a regular stick pin and hung a second strip from the one already hanging from the ceiling by sticking the pin into the side of the base, not the bottom, the bottom is too thin to hold it but if you stick it in the side, near the bottom it holds great and now you have two connected that span from the ceiling to about waist level so keep that in mind when doubling them up so as not to place them where you will be bumping into them as they are quite sticky. I really don't like to get less than positive reviews but don't waste your money on this. If you don't like using fly paper then do one of the DIY tricks from youtube with a plastic cup, apple cider, and a bit of saran wrap.
